text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a surprise move yesterday, Canadian Conrad Black, reportedly frustrated with the federal government's 25 percent limit on foreign ownership of Australian media companies, sold his Telegraph Group's 25 percent stake in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd to New Zealand company Brierley Investments Ltd for A$553 million. Page 1.

As investors flocked to the prospect of high-yield exposure to toll roads, railways and telecommunications, the Infrastructure Trust of Australia, the country's first listed infrastructure investment vehicle, made a strong debut on the stockmarket, with units listing at A$1.40, a 40 percent premium over their issue price of A$1.00 Page 1.

Following strong opposition from industry and Tasmanian Independent Senator Brian Harradine, Federal Treasurer Peter Costello and Industry Minister John Moore have issued a joint statement indicating the fovernment will back away from its hardline strategy to scrap assistance to the shipbuilding and book publishing industries. Page 3.

Telstra and IBM have joined Australia Post and Optus in the race for early dominance in the market for certifying electronic transactions by announcing a joint initiative to verify online transactions - a crucial part of the Australian market that could total more than A$100 billion in five years. Page 3.

Brierley Investments Ltd executive director Rod Price said last night there was no comparison between his company's new 25 percent shareholding in publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd and its recent short-term investment in New Zealand newspaper group Wilson & Horton, saying the Fairfax stake is a long-term investment. Page 17.

Speaking at a Sydney demonstration of Formulab Neuronetics Corp's main products - the Richter computer, neurocard and software - Formulab finance director Ken King said yesterday 95 percent of the company's revenue was derived from sales to Singapore's Goldtron group. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following the announcement last Monday that Dennis Eck would be replacing Peter Bartels on January 1 as Coles Myer chief executive, the giant retailer's stock has gained 30 cents, or 6.5 percent. The shares approached a three-year high yesterday, taking to A$320 million the gain in the company's market value since the announcement. Page 19.

In a move unlikely to affect either the commercial or defence sectors in Australia and New Zealand, Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp yesterday finalised a A$16.8 billion deal to create the world's biggest aerospace company and the United States' largest exporter. Page 19.

Despite meeting with senior Australian Broadcasting Authority officials yesterday and reaffirming its support for a float of the Ten Group Ltd, CanWest Global Communications Inc CWW.TO has failed to allay ABA concerns about the Canadian company's influence over the network. Page 21.

Drilling results released yesterday from Newcrest Mining Ltd's Cadia Ridgeway prospect near Orange in New South Wales show what appears to be a substantial high-grade mineralised zone. The exciting high-grade gold and copper intersections could result in significant upgrading of the new mine, which produces low-grade gold and copper. Page 21.

According to the ANZ Banking Group's 1996 annual report, released yesterday, its highest paid director - presumed to be chief executive Don Mercer - received a pay rise of around 25 percent, taking his annual salary beyond the A$1 million mark. He received between A$1 million and A$1.01 million in the year to September 30. Page 21.

Market observers are predicting that despite a push by Australian producers for iron ore and coal price increases during talks to resume in Tokyo today, they are unlikely to see a second annual price increase from Japan's huge steel mills after winning a six percent increase for fine ore and a five percent increase for lump ore in 1996. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

CanWest Global Communications chairman and major shareholder Izzy Asper faces further investigation over his recent share dealings in The Ten Group, despite having met with the Australian Broadcasting Authority yesterday to outline detailed plans for a sell-down. Page 25.

Former Bond Corp executive Tony Oates remains in a Polish jail where he has spent the last two months awaiting Australian extradition proceedings relating to the A$1 billion Bell Resources fraud case after failing to overturn a court decision refusing him bail. Page 25.

St George executives anxious to win overwhelming Advance Bank shareholder approval for the takeover at the December 23 meeting will be disheartened by the recent plunge in St George's share price, which could wipe more than A$50 million or 2.5 percent of the takeover offer. St George plummeted 78 cents on December 6 to A$7.82 and has fallen as low as A$7.70 before closing yesterday at A$7.74. Page 25.

While most retailers say the Christmas trading season is following the same course as last year, David Jones chairman Dick Warburton has noted a change in customers' style of shopping, with gift vouchers and sets, particularly in cosmetics, proving to be he biggest sellers during the Christmas period. Warburton says people are waiting for the post-Christmas sales before having a big spend. Page 25.

Wesfarmers Dalgety, Elders Australia and Wool International have formed a A$100 million joint venture, Global Wool Ltd, in an effort to regain the Australian wool industry's position among world competitors. Under the scheme, being reviewed by the Austraian Competition and Consumer Commission, Dalgety, Wesfarmers and Elders will merge wool handling and marketing services. Page 27.

Following an investigation by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission into claims from Perth-based mortgage originator WA Home Loans that its products and services were sledged by staff at the Bank of Western Australia, BankWest has been forced to admit that it gave customers incorrect information about its competitors. Page 27.
THE AGE

Analysts believe Brierley Investments Ltd is gambling on the same potential changes to media ownership laws as Conrad Black was before he sold BIL 20 percent of the ordinary shares and 18 percent of the debentures on issue in publisher John Fairfax. While Back grew tired of waiting for the federal government to act on media ownership laws, BIL can afford the time and the money. Page C1.

Since the 1980s, New Zealand-based Brierley Investments Limited has emerged as a more cautious and long-term investor, now New Zealand's fourth-biggest corporate with a market capitalisation of more than A$3 billion. BIL's biggest assets are in travel and leisure but it is also the third biggest shareholder in retailing giant Coles Myer and owns the Vox Group. Page C1.

As part of its plans to become the world's biggest film exhibitor by 2000, Village Roadshow has acquired a half-interest in the Sydney-based Yoram Gross Film Studios. Yoram Gross has produced such award-winning animated titles as Blinky Bill and Dot and the Kangaroo and has sold its classics in 85 countries, winning more than 80 awards. Page C2.

A taskforce is in the midst of a three-month study into how the Normandy group should establish itself as a globally rated stock. A North American listing is the expected course of action, with a high profile there likely to deliver the share-price re-rating that was meant to follow Normandy's buyout of the minorities in PosGold and GMK and its partially successful bid for North Flinders. Page C3.

New South Wales Treasurer Michael Egan said yesterday the federal government's insistence that submissions to a review of business programmes be received by February and a draft report provided a month later left the way open for new programme slashing in the May Budget. Page C3.

The government has made a deal with the two independent senators that will see the book bounty and the shipbuilding bounty extended into 1997 in return for the senators agreeing to halve the 150 percent research and development tax concession and exclude syndicated R&D schemes from tax concessions. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
